To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 150-kbp region of mouse chromosome (Chr) 16 is sytenic to the DiGeorg, velocardioficial syndrome (DGS/VCFS) minimal critical region.

a region of mouse chromosome (Chr) 16 is sytenic to the Di George, velocardio-facial syndrome (DGS/VCFS) minimal critical region (MCR) and that the genes in this region may be involved in the pathogenesis of DGS/VCF.
we have identified seven genes in a region of mouse chromosome (Chr) 16 that is syntenic with the minimal critical region of 22q.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the DGS/VCSF minimal critical region and the identification of the gene(s) responsible for the syndrome.
the identification, characterization, and mapping of genes that are syntenic to 22q11 and that are likely to be involved in the etiology of DGS/VCSF.
the genetic and molecular basis of a syndrome of developmental abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this region of mouse chromosome is syntenic with the DGS/VCSF minimal critical region.
a 150-kB region of chromosome 10 is syntenic with the DiGeorge, VCFS critical region of chromosome 22.
the region of mouse chromosome (16) that is syntenic with human chromosome 22q is the minimal critical region that is associated with the DiGeorge/velocardiofacial syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 150-kb mouse region is syntenic with a 200-kb region of human 22q11, which includes 7 genes, 3 of which have human homologues.
this region of mouse Chr 16 is sytenic with the DGS/VCSF minimal critical region on human 22q11.

we identified a region on mouse chromosome that is syntenic with the human chromosome region 22q11 that is commonly deleted in patients with DiGeorge syndrome (DGS) and velocardiofacia syndrome (VCFS) and identified seven genes in this syntenic region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse is a powerful model for studying human genetic diseases.
mouse chromosome 16 contains a region of synteny with human chromosome 22q, which may be a useful resource in the search for genes involved in DGS/22q11.

the DiGeorge/velocardiofacial syndrome (DGS/VCFS), a human congenital malformation syndrome characterized by multiple cranial and cardiac defects, results from haploinsufficiency of a region of chromosome 22 (22q11.23) that has been shown to be syntenic to a region on chromosome 16 of the mouse.
